hero.headline: Trump names housing finance chief Bill Pulte as acting intelligence director
hero.body:
President Trump appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who departed from the role last month. The decision sparked immediate criticism from Democrats and concern from Republicans about Pulte's suitability for the position.

Pulte brings no known national security or intelligence experience to the role. His background is centered on housing finance and real estate, including his leadership of the FHFA, which regulates government-backed mortgage lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Trump announced the appointment on his Truth Social platform, stating that Pulte has "deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America." Pulte will retain his position at the FHFA while serving as acting intelligence director.

The appointment has raised concerns among both parties. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters that the intelligence community needs professionals and warned that if Pulte is nominated for permanent confirmation, he will face "a lengthy road ahead" including hearings and a confirmation process.

The concern extends beyond Pulte's lack of experience. During his tenure at the FHFA, Pulte has made public allegations against Trump's political opponents, including accusations of mortgage fraud against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, who has denied wrongdoing. Thune's comments suggesting the need for professionals rather than a "weaponized" intelligence director appeared to reference these concerns about Pulte pursuing Trump's rivals.

Pulte comes from significant wealth as the heir to PulteGroup, a major home construction company founded by his grandfather. However, he no longer holds any official connection to the company after being pushed off the board in 2020. His own family has publicly distanced itself from him. The PulteGroup's charitable foundation issued a 2023 statement clarifying that Pulte does not represent the organization and does not serve in any capacity for it.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence oversees the nation's intelligence community, coordinating information from agencies including the CIA, NSA, and FBI. The position typically requires extensive experience in national security operations. The office coordinates threat assessments and national security briefings across multiple federal intelligence agencies.

Gabbard's departure left the intelligence director position vacant. Trump had been discussing replacing her with cabinet members as early as April, according to people briefed on the discussions. Gabbard's time in the role was marked by conflict, including being largely sidelined during Trump's foreign policy actions concerning Venezuela and Iran.

The acting appointment allows Pulte to serve temporarily without Senate confirmation, though a permanent director would require approval from the Senate Intelligence Committee and full Senate vote.

cards.headline: 20,000 sailors trapped in Strait of Hormuz blockade face mounting stress
cards.teaser: Seafarers remain stuck in the Iran war zone after months of blockade, with uncertainty weighing heavily on crews.
cards.body:
Around 20,000 seafarers remain trapped by the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, with crews reporting stress and exhaustion after months in the Iran war zone. The prolonged standoff has left commercial vessels unable to transit the strategic waterway.

The uncertainty surrounding when the blockade might end has taken a heavy toll on the sailors. Many have been separated from their families for extended periods while their ships remain stuck in the region.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio details US demands as Iran peace talks stall
cards.teaser: Rubio faced questioning from senators about Iran negotiations, as well as policies on Ukraine, Taiwan, and other foreign policy matters.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate about the administration's approach to stalled Iran peace negotiations, outlining US demands in the talks.

During the hearing, Democratic senators including Senator Shaheen pressed Rubio on various foreign policy matters. Rubio also addressed questions about Taiwan, Ebola response, and maritime incidents involving boat strikes.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Lebanon Strikes as Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to maintain the campaign against Hezbollah even as diplomatic meetings proceed.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue military operations against Hezbollah while Lebanese and Israeli officials held peace talks in Washington. Israel has maintained strikes in southern Lebanon but has not targeted Beirut following a US-announced deal.

The partial ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah appears to be holding despite the ongoing Israeli campaign in the south. Meanwhile, Iran halted talks with the U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: US Missile Strikes Iran-Bound Oil Tanker After Crew Ignores Warnings
cards.teaser: The US military hit a vessel's engine room after repeated attempts to communicate went unanswered.
cards.body:
The US military fired a missile at an oil tanker headed to Iran after the crew failed to respond to repeated warnings. The strike hit the vessel's engine room.

The attack reflects escalating US military involvement in regional shipping amid rising tensions. By targeting the tanker's propulsion system rather than destroying it outright, the US appeared aimed at disabling the vessel.

cards.headline: Trump Calls Canada 51st State Again Hours Before Trade Talks
Trump administration abandons $1.8 billion compensation fund
cards.teaser: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision to drop the fund amid criticism from Republican lawmakers.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Trump administration will abandon a $1.8 billion compensation fund. The decision follows opposition from senior Republican lawmakers in Congress who raised concerns about the fund.

The move represents a policy reversal for the administration. Blanche's announcement came in response to the pushback from members of his own party, though he did not elaborate extensively on the specific reasons behind the decision.

hero.headline: Russian Attack on Ukraine Kills at Least 22, Destroys Apartment Building
hero.body:
A Russian missile and drone attack across Ukraine killed at least 22 people and wounded 138 others, according to Ukrainian officials. The overnight bombardment struck multiple cities in one of the deadliest offensives in recent months, with particular devastation in the western city of Ternopil, where apartment buildings were heavily damaged.

Ukrainian interior minister Ihor Klymenko reported that an upper floor of a residential building in Ternopil was torn away in the assault. "The main thing is to find those who could still be under the rubble," Klymenko said on Telegram as emergency crews worked through the night searching for survivors. He noted that flames engulfed the building instantly, with residents attempting to escape through windows.

Russia employed an enormous arsenal in the assault, firing 476 drones and 48 missiles at Ukrainian targets. The strikes hit energy and transport infrastructure across multiple regions, forcing emergency power cuts as residents faced frigid temperatures. Explosions were reported in the western city of Lviv and the northwestern city of Kharkiv, while residents in Kyiv sought shelter in metro stations.

The attack comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Turkey for peace negotiations with Russia. He has called on allies to intensify pressure on Moscow, including through additional sanctions and military aid. "Every brazen attack against ordinary life shows that the pressure on Russia is insufficient," Zelenskyy said. "Effective sanctions and assistance to Ukraine can change this."

The timing of the bombardment coincides with reports of a new peace proposal being quietly developed by American and Russian officials. According to reports, the draft plan would require Ukraine to surrender territory it controls in the east and significantly reduce its military size. Zelenskyy has previously rejected such conditions as non-starters.

The attack underscores Ukraine's continued vulnerability to Russian aerial assaults despite air defense systems provided by Western allies. Ukrainian officials have repeatedly requested additional air-defense missiles to protect population centers from such strikes.

The death toll may rise as rescue operations continue. Many people remain listed as missing in the rubble of destroyed residential buildings. The scale of the assault, involving hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles, demonstrates Russia's sustained capacity to launch large-scale coordinated attacks deep into Ukrainian territory.

The bombardment also coincides with heightened tensions in the broader region. Poland's foreign minister described a recent sabotage attack on Polish rail infrastructure as "an act of state terrorism" ordered by Russia, and Poland announced it was closing its last remaining Russian consulate in response.

cards.headline: US Missile Strikes Iran-Bound Oil Tanker After Crew Ignores Warnings
cards.teaser: The US military hit a vessel's engine room after repeated attempts to communicate went unanswered.

The US military fired a missile at an oil tanker headed to Iran after the crew failed to respond to repeated warnings. The strike hit the vessel's engine room.

The attack reflects escalating US military involvement in regional shipping amid rising tensions. By targeting the tanker's propulsion system rather than destroying it outright, the US appeared aimed at disabling the vessel.

cards.headline: Ship Hit by Projectiles at Iraqi Port as Iran Claims Responsibility
cards.teaser: A Panama-flagged vessel exploded near Iraq's Umm Qasr port in an attack Iran says it carried out.
cards.body:
A Panama-flagged container ship operated by MSC was struck by projectiles near Umm Qasr in Iraq, igniting a fire on board. Iran has claimed responsibility for the attack.

The strike represents the second attack on the MSC vessel, according to shipping industry reports. The incident underscores escalating regional tensions affecting maritime traffic in the Gulf.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Warned of Strait of Hormuz Threat, Failed to Heed Advice
cards.teaser: Iran repeatedly threatened to close the waterway over two decades, but the president underestimated the country's capability.
cards.body:
President Trump underestimated Iran's ability to close the Strait of Hormuz despite warnings from war games and intelligence assessments conducted over the past two decades. Iran had repeatedly threatened to shut down the critical waterway.

The failure to heed these warnings has left the administration unprepared for Iran's current actions in the region. The strait is a vital chokepoint for global oil shipments, and its closure or disruption has significant economic consequences.

cards.headline: British Police Under Investigation After Student Dies While Handcuffed
cards.teaser: Henry Nowak was restrained by officers as he was dying, sparking outrage and political controversy.
cards.body:
British authorities are investigating police officers who handcuffed student Henry Nowak while he was dying. Footage of the arrest has drawn scrutiny from the prime minister, who said it raises serious questions about police conduct.

The case has become increasingly politicized in the UK, sparking broader debate about how police apply the law and handle arrests.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Lebanon Strikes as Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to maintain the campaign against Hezbollah even as diplomatic meetings proceed.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to continue military operations against Hezbollah while Lebanese and Israeli officials held peace talks in Washington. Israel has maintained strikes in southern Lebanon but has not targeted Beirut following a US-announced deal.

The partial ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah appears to be holding despite the ongoing Israeli campaign in the south. Meanwhile, Iran halted talks with the U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Kenya Court Delays US Ebola Quarantine Unit Plans Amid Protests
cards.teaser: A court ruling further postponed the Trump administration's proposed facility for Americans exposed to the virus.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has delayed the Trump administration's plan to establish an Ebola quarantine facility for US citizens at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki, about 120 miles from Nairobi. The proposed center would house Americans exposed to the virus during outbreaks.

Local residents oppose the project, arguing it poses health risks to their community despite Kenya having no known Ebola cases. Critics view the plan as a double standard, with residents like taxi driver Charles Mathenge asserting that countries should quarantine their own citizens rather than sending them abroad. The legal challenges and public demonstrations have stalled the initiative.

hero.headline: Trump administration abandons $1.8 billion compensation fund
hero.teaser: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision to drop the fund amid criticism from Republican lawmakers.
hero.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Trump administration will abandon a $1.8 billion compensation fund. The decision follows opposition from senior Republican lawmakers in Congress who raised concerns about the fund.

The move represents a policy reversal for the administration. Blanche's announcement came in response to the pushback from members of his own party, though he did not elaborate extensively on the specific reasons behind the decision.

cards.headline: Voters cast ballots in six-state primary including California governor's race
cards.teaser: Primary elections took place in California, Iowa, New Jersey, and three other states, with polls closing throughout the evening.
cards.body:
Primary elections took place across six states on Tuesday, with California, Iowa, New Jersey, South Dakota, New Mexico, and Montana all holding contests. The races included closely watched positions such as California's governor and Los Angeles mayor.

The California governor's race emerged as particularly significant, with Democrats facing a choice between different visions for the state. Xavier Becerra, the establishment favorite, represents a more traditional corporate-friendly approach to governing the nation's fourth-largest economy. Other candidates in the field offered contrasting political directions for the state's future.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio details US demands as Iran peace talks stall
cards.teaser: Rubio faced questioning from senators about Iran negotiations, as well as policies on Ukraine, Taiwan, and other foreign policy matters.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate about the administration's approach to stalled Iran peace negotiations, outlining US demands in the talks.

During the hearing, Democratic senators including Senator Shaheen pressed Rubio on various foreign policy matters. Rubio also addressed questions about Taiwan, Ebola response, and maritime incidents involving boat strikes.

cards.body:

cards.headline: Warmer than normal summer forecast increases heatwave likelihood
cards.teaser: Long-range forecasts point to warmer and drier conditions compared to average for the coming summer months.
cards.body:
Long-range summer forecasts indicate that warmer and drier conditions are expected compared to seasonal averages. According to the outlook, this pattern significantly increases the likelihood of heatwaves during the coming months.

Weather forecasters have identified these broader climate patterns for the season and issued the outlook to help communities and individuals prepare for the potentially challenging summer conditions ahead.

cards.headline: Research links regular weight training to reduced risk of early death
cards.teaser: New research suggests that consistent strength training can significantly lower the risk of premature mortality.
cards.body:
Regular weight training can significantly reduce the risk of early death, according to new research findings. The study adds to growing evidence about the health benefits of strength training beyond cardiovascular exercise.

The research suggests that incorporating weight training into regular fitness routines provides measurable longevity benefits. The findings could influence public health recommendations about exercise and physical activity.

cards.headline: Report finds three quarters of workers lack savings for moderate retirement
cards.teaser: A new analysis suggests most workers are not on track to afford a moderate lifestyle in retirement.
cards.body:
Three quarters of workers are not on track to achieve a moderate pension income in retirement, according to a newly published report. The analysis defines a moderate lifestyle as costing £32,700 annually for one person and £45,400 for two people.

The findings reveal a significant shortfall between the savings most workers have accumulated and the income required to maintain a comfortable standard of living in retirement.

hero.headline: SpaceX targets $1.75 trillion valuation in public offering next week
hero.body:
SpaceX Merges with xAI Ahead of Major Public Offering

SpaceX has acquired Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company xAI in a $1.25 trillion merger that combines the aerospace firm with AI capabilities, chatbot technology, and the social media platform X. The deal values SpaceX at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion, positioning the combined entity for a stock market listing expected to value it well above $1 trillion.

The merger consolidates multiple parts of Musk's business empire as SpaceX prepares to go public. According to the companies' joint announcement, the combination creates "the most ambitious, vertically-integrated innovation engine on (and off) Earth, with AI, rockets, space-based internet, direct-to-mobile device communications and the world's foremost real-time information and free speech platform."

The deal reflects Musk's strategy of developing space-based datacenters powered by solar satellites to support artificial intelligence operations. The companies stated that current AI advances depend on massive terrestrial datacenters requiring enormous amounts of power and cooling. "Global electricity demand for AI simply cannot be met with terrestrial solutions, even in the near term, without imposing hardship on communities and the environment," the announcement said. "In the long term, space-based AI is obviously the only way to scale."

The public offering is expected for early summer, timed to coincide with a planetary alignment and Musk's 55th birthday on June 28, when Jupiter and Venus will appear in close proximity.

SpaceX's valuation has grown substantially. In December, the company sent a letter to investors indicating an expected value of $800 billion. The new merger agreement reflects a significant increase from that figure. Meanwhile, xAI's valuation has also risen dramatically during the AI boom, with the company announcing a $20 billion Series E fundraise last month that valued it at $230 billion.

Musk confirmed the acquisition on Monday with a brief "yes" response to a post on X referencing merger reports that Reuters had first disclosed.

The deal comes as multiple major technology companies prepare for public offerings. Anthropic, the AI firm behind the Claude chatbot, has confidentially filed for an initial public offering and announced raising $65 billion in funding that valued the company at $965 billion. OpenAI is also expected to pursue a public listing this year.

Speculation about the SpaceX-xAI merger has circulated for days ahead of Monday's announcement. The news provides positive momentum for Musk following Tesla's recent earnings report showing declining revenues and a struggling automotive business. The combined SpaceX-xAI entity will integrate Starlink satellite internet, rocket launches for commercial and government customers, and AI infrastructure into a single operation preparing for Wall Street debut.

cards.headline: Seven states sue Trump administration over $1 billion offshore wind farm deal
cards.teaser: A coalition of states filed suit after the administration paid a French company to halt an offshore wind project.
cards.body:
Seven states, led by New York, have filed a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration's deal to halt an offshore wind farm project. The agreement involves paying French energy company TotalEnergies approximately $1 billion to abandon construction.

The states argue the payment arrangement undermines renewable energy development along the East Coast. The legal challenge targets how the administration structured the deal to stop the offshore wind initiative.

cards.headline: Fed Chair Warsh appoints two conservative policy advisers
cards.teaser: The Federal Reserve chairman made his first personnel moves, selecting two veterans of conservative policy circles.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh named two conservative policy veterans as interim advisers, marking his first appointments at the central bank. The hires include an author who contributed to Project 2025, a conservative policy blueprint.

The advisers are Paul Winfree and Stephen Heil, both with backgrounds in conservative economic policy. Warsh pledged to follow what he described as the best of the Fed's traditions while pursuing changes to the institution. The appointments signal the new chairman's approach to staffing the central bank.

cards.headline: S&P 500 closes above 7,600 for first time as AI stocks climb
cards.teaser: The stock index set another record as technology companies focused on artificial intelligence continued advancing.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 closed above 7,600 for the first time, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average gaining over 200 points as both indexes reached fresh records. Stock futures showed little movement following the close.

Artificial intelligence stocks led the market's advance, continuing momentum that has driven gains throughout the year. Technology companies have powered the broader market higher, pushing valuations to new peaks.

cards.headline: Colorado tightens oversight of Uber and Lyft after safety investigation
cards.teaser: The state enacted legislation increasing scrutiny of ride-hailing companies following reports of unreported assaults.
cards.body:
Colorado enacted a law increasing regulatory oversight of Uber and Lyft, citing findings from a New York Times investigation. The investigation found that Uber received reports of sexual assault or sexual misconduct far more frequently than the company had publicly disclosed.

The new legislation strengthens state scrutiny of safety practices at ride-hailing companies operating in Colorado. Lawmakers cited the need for greater transparency about passenger safety incidents and more robust reporting requirements for companies in the industry.

cards.headline: MSC cargo ship struck by projectiles at Iraqi port
cards.teaser: Two projectiles hit a vessel owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company, underscoring risks as US and Iran negotiate.
cards.body:
A ship owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company was struck by two projectiles while at an Iraqi port. The attack occurred as the United States and Iran attempt to negotiate terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global shipping.

The incident highlights continuing threats to commercial vessels in the region despite ongoing diplomatic efforts. The strait has been a focal point of tensions affecting international maritime trade, with attacks on shipping raising insurance costs and forcing some vessels to seek alternative routes.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret shares hit record high on bra sales turnaround
cards.teaser: The retailer's stock soared 50 percent in its best single-day performance ever after reporting strong results.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret shares jumped to a record high after the company reported that its bra sales strategy drove a turnaround in performance. The stock surged 50 percent, marking the best single day in the company's trading history.

The retailer issued upbeat annual forecasts based on strength across its core product lines. Wall Street analysts noted that improved bra sales powered the reversal after years of declining market share. The company's focus on fit and product quality appears to be resonating with customers.

hero.headline: Microsoft introduces Scout, an AI assistant designed to keep users engaged
hero.body:
Microsoft unveiled Scout, a new AI assistant functioning as a personal agent for office workers, at its Build 2026 developer conference. Internal documents obtained by 404 Media reveal the company aims to make people addicted to the assistant, which operates continuously like an executive assistant that never logs off.

Scout represents Microsoft's push into AI-powered personal productivity tools designed to help office workers manage tasks and information throughout their workday. The always-on nature of the assistant means it continuously monitors and responds to user needs, a feature Microsoft promotes as beneficial for productivity. The company is marketing Scout as a coworker available at all times, distinguishing it from tools requiring explicit activation.

The internal documents suggesting Microsoft wants users to become addicted to Scout raise questions about the design philosophy behind AI assistants and how technology companies approach user engagement. The always-on monitoring capability represents a shift in how companies are designing AI tools for daily workflows. However, Microsoft has not provided details on privacy protections or how user data will be handled by the continuously active assistant.

At Build 2026, Microsoft announced several other AI initiatives alongside Scout. The company introduced new proprietary AI models designed to reduce its reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. This move reflects Microsoft's broader strategy of offering more proprietary AI solutions rather than depending on external partnerships.

The Scout launch comes as major technology companies compete to embed AI assistants into daily workflows and work environments. Microsoft's approach of keeping the assistant constantly active differs from existing tools that require manual activation by users. The company is positioning itself to offer comprehensive AI solutions across its product ecosystem.

Scout's introduction also coincides with Microsoft's testing of other AI hardware and software. The company is testing a wearable AI gadget aimed at office workers, expanding its approach beyond traditional software interfaces. Microsoft also unveiled Project Solara, an Android operating system designed specifically for agents rather than traditional apps, signaling the company's vision for how AI agents will integrate into devices and workflows.

These announcements demonstrate Microsoft's commitment to integrating AI across its entire product lineup, from Windows operating systems to cloud services and wearable devices. The company is betting that AI agents like Scout will become essential tools for office productivity, with the always-on assistant model becoming standard rather than optional.

The focus on addiction and engagement in Scout's design documents reflects broader industry trends around AI assistant adoption and user retention. As companies compete in the AI market, questions about responsible design practices and user autonomy continue to emerge alongside announcements of new capabilities and features.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Project Solara, an Android operating system built for AI agents
cards.teaser: The company is developing an Android-based operating system designed around AI agents rather than traditional apps.
cards.body:
Microsoft revealed Project Solara, an Android-based operating system that prioritizes AI agents over traditional applications. The system represents a shift in how operating systems are designed, focusing on autonomous software agents that can perform tasks rather than requiring users to navigate individual apps.

The announcement came at the Microsoft Build 2026 developer conference, where the company showcased multiple AI initiatives. Ars Technica reported that the operating system is designed specifically for agents instead of apps, suggesting Microsoft is betting on a future where AI handles more tasks autonomously. The move comes as Microsoft attempts to compete in areas where it previously missed opportunities, particularly in mobile app ecosystems.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Linux tools and RTX Spark desktop for Windows developers
cards.teaser: The company unveiled new developer tools at its Build conference, including Linux integration and new hardware.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced new tools for Windows developers at its Build 2026 conference, including expanded Linux capabilities and a desktop called RTX Spark. The announcements combined both hardware and software updates aimed at improving the development experience on Windows.

The RTX Spark desktop represents a hardware offering from Microsoft, though specific technical details about the system were not provided in the initial announcement. The Linux tools indicate Microsoft's continued efforts to make Windows a more versatile platform for developers who work across different operating systems.

cards.headline: Microsoft testing wearable AI device for office workers
cards.teaser: The company is developing a wearable gadget with AI capabilities aimed at workplace productivity.
cards.body:
Microsoft is testing a wearable AI device designed for office workers, according to BBC reporting. The gadget represents another avenue for the company's AI strategy beyond software applications and desktop computers.

The wearable device is currently in testing phases, with Microsoft exploring how AI can be integrated into physical devices worn by employees. The announcement comes alongside other AI initiatives from Microsoft, including new models designed to reduce the company's dependence on OpenAI and lower costs for developers using its AI services.

cards.headline: Ring faces lawsuit over facial recognition scanning of visitors and passersby
cards.teaser: A lawsuit claims Amazon-owned Ring cameras scan faces and use AI to identify people without consent.
cards.body:
A class action lawsuit filed in Seattle by Virginia resident Charles Sigwalt alleges that Amazon's Ring division scans and stores faces of passersby without their consent through its Familiar Faces feature. The complaint claims Ring's home security cameras capture and analyze the faces of people near properties where Ring devices are installed, extending surveillance beyond property owners and residents.

The legal action seeks compensation for Americans whose facial images were scanned without permission. The lawsuit raises broader questions about privacy and consent when surveillance technology captures data from individuals who have not agreed to be monitored.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera pursues funding at $12 billion valuation despite losses
cards.teaser: The company is nearing a $300 million funding round that would value it at 80 times its annual recurring revenue.
cards.body:
Cyera, a cybersecurity company, is close to securing a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners that would value the firm at $12 billion. The valuation represents 80 times the company's annual recurring revenue, an unusually high multiple for a business still operating at a loss.

The funding round reflects continued investor appetite for cybersecurity companies despite broader market conditions. Cyera's ability to command such a high valuation while unprofitable indicates investor confidence in the company's growth potential and market position in the data security sector.

cards.headline: Male bowerbirds now using human objects to attract mates
cards.teaser: The birds are incorporating bright human-made items into their courtship displays.
cards.body:
Male bowerbirds are increasingly using colorful human-made objects in their elaborate courtship displays to attract female mates. The behavior demonstrates how wildlife is adapting to human presence in unexpected ways.

Researchers noted that the incorporation of manufactured items into bowerbird displays serves as a reminder of how human activity is changing the natural world in ways scientists did not anticipate. Bowerbirds are known for building elaborate structures and decorating them with objects to impress potential mates, and they have now expanded their collection to include items produced by humans.

hero.headline: Stephen Curry signs $400 million endorsement deal with Li-Ning
hero.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has signed a 10-year endorsement contract with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning worth $400 million, according to sources. The deal marks one of the largest athlete endorsement agreements in basketball history and represents a significant shift in the global sneaker market.

Curry's move to Li-Ning ends a long relationship with major Western athletic brands and signals the growing influence of Chinese sportswear companies in signing top-tier NBA talent. The $400 million total over a decade averages $40 million annually, placing Curry among the highest-paid athletes in endorsement earnings across all sports.

Li-Ning, founded by Chinese Olympic gymnast Li Ning in 1990, has been expanding its presence in international basketball markets in recent years. The company has previously signed NBA players but never at the superstar caliber of Curry, a four-time NBA champion and two-time league MVP who revolutionized basketball with his three-point shooting.

The deal comes as Chinese sportswear brands compete more aggressively with established American companies for endorsement partnerships with elite athletes. Li-Ning's investment in Curry reflects both the player's global appeal and the company's ambitions to expand its footprint in North American and international markets.

Curry, 38, remains one of the most marketable athletes in professional sports despite being in the latter stages of his playing career. His popularity extends well beyond the United States, particularly in China, where basketball enjoys massive popularity and the NBA has cultivated a substantial fan base over decades. The length and value of the contract suggest Li-Ning views Curry as a brand ambassador who can help the company grow even after his playing days end.

cards.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett in trade with Browns
cards.teaser: Coach Sean McVay compared the acquisition of the star defensive end to the trade that brought Matthew Stafford to Los Angeles.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Rams acquired two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in a blockbuster trade. The Rams sent linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to Cleveland in the deal. Garrett, 30, is a seven-time Pro Bowl selection who set an NFL single-season sacks record with 23 in 2025.

Since being drafted first overall by the Browns in 2017, Garrett has established himself as one of the league's elite defensive players. He leads all players from that span with 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures, and 149 tackles for loss. Coach Sean McVay said the Rams were aggressive in pursuing Garrett, comparing the opportunity to their acquisition of quarterback Matthew Stafford.

cards.headline: Falcons extend Drake London with four-year, $141 million contract
cards.teaser: The star wide receiver agreed to terms on the extension, making him one of the highest-paid players at his position.
cards.body:
The Atlanta Falcons and wide receiver Drake London have agreed to a four-year, $141 million contract extension, according to his agent Andrew Kessler. The deal solidifies London's future with the team as a key offensive weapon.

The extension places London among the NFL's highest-paid receivers, reflecting his status as one of the league's premier pass catchers since joining Atlanta.

cards.headline: Steelers sign Nick Herbig to four-year, $100 million extension
cards.teaser: The linebacker agreed to the deal after sitting out individual drills during mandatory minicamp.
cards.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Nick Herbig has agreed to a four-year, $100 million contract extension with $42 million guaranteed, according to sources at NFL Network and ESPN. The deal came after Herbig sat out individual drills during the team's mandatory minicamp.

The extension keeps Herbig under contract through the 2030 season and establishes him among the NFL's highest-paid linebackers, recognizing his emergence as a key defensive contributor for Pittsburgh.

cards.headline: Mike Evans signs with 49ers, leaving Buccaneers after long tenure
cards.teaser: Teammate Chris Godwin Jr. said he learned of the move on social media and initially thought it was fake.
cards.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. learned that teammate Mike Evans was signing with the San Francisco 49ers through social media. Godwin said he did not believe the news was real until quarterback Baker Mayfield texted him a sad face emoji.

Evans' departure ends a long run with the Buccaneers, where he established himself as one of the franchise's most productive receivers. The move to San Francisco pairs Evans with a contending team looking to add veteran receiving talent.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown, teammates express relief
cards.teaser: Philadelphia's left tackle said he was glad the saga was over after Brown's departure to another team.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation about his future. In the deal, the Eagles received a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 for the three-time Pro Bowl selection.

Brown's teammates offered mixed reactions to his departure. While some expressed a sense of loss, others felt relief that the uncertainty had finally concluded. The team's left tackle was among those glad the situation was resolved, saying the saga was over.

cards.headline: NHL All-Star Game to feature international team format
cards.teaser: Commissioner Gary Bettman announced the change before Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
NHL commissioner Gary Bettman announced that All-Star Weekend will adopt an international team format during his state of the league address before Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final on Tuesday. The decision was influenced by the popularity of the 4 Nations Face-Off and Winter Olympics.

The shift marks a significant change from the traditional All-Star Game structure, moving toward international competition that has resonated with hockey fans.

hero.headline: Ernest Chambers, The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour Showrunner, Dies at 97
hero.teaser: The television producer and writer known for variety shows died at his Los Angeles home following a brief illness.
hero.body:
Ernest Chambers, the writer and producer known for variety television shows including "The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour" and "Click," died on May 28 at his home in Los Angeles following a brief illness. He was 97 years old.

Chambers produced, wrote and executive produced over 1,000 hours of television during his 50-year career in the industry. His work earned him 11 Emmy nominations throughout his time in television production, cementing his reputation as a significant figure in the variety show format during its peak years on American television.

cards.headline: Peabo Bryson, Grammy-Winning Singer Behind Disney Ballads, Dies at 75
cards.teaser: Peabo Bryson, the Grammy-winning singer known for performing iconic Disney film songs including "Beauty and the Beast" and "A Whole New World," has died at age .
cards.body:
Peabo Bryson, the two-time Grammy Award-winning R&B singer, has died at age 75. His family announced his death on Tuesday, days after he suffered a stroke.

Bryson was best known for his iconic Disney film duets, including "Beauty and the Beast" with Regina Belle from the 1991 animated film and "A Whole New World" with Celine Dion from "Aladdin." His powerful vocal style made him a defining voice of romantic ballads during the 1990s Disney renaissance and established him as a prominent figure in R&B music.

cards.headline: NBC Cancels The Hunting Party After Two Seasons
cards.teaser: The crime drama starring Melissa Roxburgh aired its final episode in May and will not return for a third season.
cards.body:
NBC has canceled "The Hunting Party" after two seasons. The crime drama's final episode aired on May 7, with Melissa Roxburgh starring as former FBI profiler Rebecca "Bex" Henderson.

The show followed Henderson leading a team of investigators tasked with hunting down dangerous criminals. Following the NBC cancellation, the series will be shopped to other networks and streaming platforms in hopes of finding a new home.

cards.headline: JioHotstar Recruits for Over 75 AI Roles to Build Dedicated Division
cards.teaser: India's largest streaming platform is building out artificial intelligence capabilities spanning engineering, production automation and creative technology.
cards.body:
JioHotstar announced it is recruiting for more than 75 artificial intelligence roles as the platform builds a dedicated AI division. The company revealed the hiring push on Wednesday, positioning the effort as a foundation for broader global expansion.

The positions span engineering, production automation and creative technology. The streamer is leveraging India's multilingual scale and engineering base as it develops AI capabilities for its platform, which remains the country's largest streaming service.

cards.headline: Wolverine Game Developers Detail Combat System and Mature Content Options
cards.teaser: Insomniac Games released new gameplay footage showing the title's approach to violence and character mechanics.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games released new gameplay footage for its upcoming "Marvel's Wolverine" game, emphasizing the mature nature of the content. Creative director Marcus Smith stated the company is planting its flag that this is a mature game, confirming the title will feature significant blood and violence.

The developers discussed new details including X-Men character cameos, a low-gore option for players who prefer less graphic content, and the claw combat system. They also addressed how the character Logan can die within the game's mechanics, offering insight into the balance between the character's healing factor and gameplay challenges.

cards.headline: Virginia Woolf's Night and Day Adapted for Screen With Haley Bennett
cards.teaser: A new film adaptation brings the author's 1919 novel to life, though reviews note an uneven execution.
cards.body:
Haley Bennett stars in a film adaptation of Virginia Woolf's 1919 novel "Night and Day." The novel weaves reflections on women's suffrage through a quasi-Shakespearean structure of romantic entanglements and rearrangements.

The adaptation has been praised for its heart but criticized for a heavy-handed approach to the source material. Translating Woolf's complex and elusive novel to screen presented significant challenges for the filmmakers.

cards.headline: Tom Holland and Zendaya Halted Spider-Man Production to Rewrite Scene
cards.teaser: The actors spoke up on the set of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" when a scene was not working, prompting a full rewrite.
cards.body:
Tom Holland revealed on Amy Poehler's "Good Hang" podcast that he and Zendaya stopped production on "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" when a scene was not working. The director sent the crew home so the scene could be rewritten, demonstrating the actors' creative input on the project.

hero.headline: Trump names housing finance chief Bill Pulte as acting intelligence director
hero.body:
President Trump appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who departed from the role last month. The decision sparked immediate criticism from Democrats and concern from Republicans about Pulte's suitability for the position.

Pulte brings no known national security or intelligence experience to the role. His background is centered on housing finance and real estate, including his leadership of the FHFA, which regulates government-backed mortgage lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Trump announced the appointment on his Truth Social platform, stating that Pulte has "deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America." Pulte will retain his position at the FHFA while serving as acting intelligence director.

The appointment has raised concerns among both parties. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters that the intelligence community needs professionals and warned that if Pulte is nominated for permanent confirmation, he will face "a lengthy road ahead" including hearings and a confirmation process.

The concern extends beyond Pulte's lack of experience. During his tenure at the FHFA, Pulte has made public allegations against Trump's political opponents, including accusations of mortgage fraud against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, who has denied wrongdoing. Thune's comments suggesting the need for professionals rather than a "weaponized" intelligence director appeared to reference these concerns about Pulte pursuing Trump's rivals.

Pulte comes from significant wealth as the heir to PulteGroup, a major home construction company founded by his grandfather. However, he no longer holds any official connection to the company after being pushed off the board in 2020. His own family has publicly distanced itself from him. The PulteGroup's charitable foundation issued a 2023 statement clarifying that Pulte does not represent the organization and does not serve in any capacity for it.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence oversees the nation's intelligence community, coordinating information from agencies including the CIA, NSA, and FBI. The position typically requires extensive experience in national security operations. The office coordinates threat assessments and national security briefings across multiple federal intelligence agencies.

Gabbard's departure left the intelligence director position vacant. Trump had been discussing replacing her with cabinet members as early as April, according to people briefed on the discussions. Gabbard's time in the role was marked by conflict, including being largely sidelined during Trump's foreign policy actions concerning Venezuela and Iran.

The acting appointment allows Pulte to serve temporarily without Senate confirmation, though a permanent director would require approval from the Senate Intelligence Committee and full Senate vote.

cards.headline: California and New Mexico hold gubernatorial primaries
cards.teaser: Voters in California and New Mexico cast ballots to select candidates to replace term-limited governors.
cards.body:
California voters selected nominees to replace Governor Gavin Newsom from a Democratic field that included Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra, along with Republican candidates Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton. Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer led the Democratic race heading into poll closings.

In New Mexico, five candidates competed for the Democratic and Republican nominations to succeed Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham: Sam Bregman, Deb Haaland, Gregg Hull, Duke Rodriguez, and Doug Turner. These primaries took place as part of a six-state primary day that also included New Jersey, South Dakota, Iowa, and Montana.

cards.headline: Illinois senators call for Chicago US attorney to resign
cards.teaser: Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth demanded Andrew Boutros step down following a failed prosecution case.
cards.body:
Senators Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth called for interim U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros to resign from his position overseeing the Northern District of Illinois. The senators accused Boutros of presiding over a federal office plagued by dysfunction and alleged misconduct following the failed Broadview Six case.

Durbin and Duckworth stated that Boutros's tenure as interim U.S. Attorney had been riddled with problems. The call for resignation represents a direct challenge from the state's two Democratic senators to the federal prosecutor leading the Chicago office.

cards.headline: Jeffries declines to endorse Debbie Wasserman Schultz reelection bid
cards.teaser: The House Democratic leader broke with his usual practice of backing all incumbents.
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he has not decided whether to support Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz's reelection campaign. The decision followed anger over Wasserman Schultz's choice to run in a majority-minority district. Jeffries is known for uniformly backing even polarizing members of his caucus.

The move stunned some of Jeffries's colleagues. One senior House Democrat said Jeffries had never withheld support from an incumbent before. When asked a different question, Jeffries declared that he stands behind every single member of the Democratic caucus, making the refusal to immediately endorse Wasserman Schultz particularly striking.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner meets with Democratic senators
cards.teaser: The candidate sought to shore up support following reports of sexually explicit messages.
cards.body:
Democratic Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner met with key party leaders in Washington on Tuesday to address mounting controversies threatening his campaign. The latest scandal involves sexually explicit text messages he sent to women outside his marriage.

Platner's candidacy has been marked by multiple problems, including previous online posts he attributed to PTSD and a covered-up Nazi tattoo. Despite these revelations, senior Democrats appeared to maintain their support for his bid to unseat Republican Senator Susan Collins, viewing the seat as central to their party's efforts to regain congressional control.

cards.headline: Rebecca Bennett wins Democratic primary in New Jersey's 7th district
cards.teaser: The former Navy helicopter pilot will challenge Republican incumbent Tom Kean Jr.
cards.body:
Democrat Rebecca Bennett won the primary race and will advance to face Republican incumbent Tom Kean Jr. in New Jersey's 7th Congressional District this fall, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Bennett previously served as a U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and officer in the Air National Guard. Kean, a two-term Republican congressman, ran unopposed in his primary and will defend his seat in the general election.

cards.headline: Democratic strategist warns Los Angeles mayor faces tough reelection
cards.teaser: Former Obama aide Jim Messina said Karen Bass should be concerned about her runoff prospects.
cards.body:
Democratic strategist Jim Messina warned that Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass should be worried about her reelection chances ahead of the California primary. Messina, who served as White House deputy chief of staff under President Obama, told reporters that Bass should be very worried regardless of which opponent makes the runoff.

The comments came as California held its primary races. Messina's warning suggested Bass faces significant challenges in her bid for a second term as mayor of the nation's second-largest city.
